prompt.brief: Design a real-time analytics dashboard that ingests streaming events, maintains queryable aggregates, refreshes visualizations automatically, and controls analytical cost and freshness.
successSignals: Define event schema, dimensions, windows, late-data policy, aggregate semantics, dashboard freshness, and tenant/query access boundaries.
Separate streaming rollups from warehouse history and interactive queries; use bounded state, pre-aggregation, caching, and query quotas.
Handle duplicates, corrections, schema evolution, dashboard refresh storms, backfills, and approximate versus exact metrics.
Explain data quality, privacy/deletion, cost controls, replay, observability, and stale/local dashboard fallback.

functional: Ingest validated events, update windowed aggregates, persist raw data, and expose SQL-backed dashboard datasets with freshness metadata.
Provide configurable charts, filters, drill-down, alerts, scheduled refresh, saved queries, exports, and tenant-scoped sharing.
Support corrections/backfills, retention/deletion, query cancellation, replay, dashboard versioning, and recovery after stream or warehouse failure.
nonFunctional: Meet p95 common dashboard query latency under five seconds and show aggregate watermark/freshness for every panel.
Serve 100k concurrent viewers and billions of events per day without a single hot key or unbounded synchronous work.
Do not lose committed state; make retries and duplicate events safe.
Degrade safely when downstream workers, caches, or external dependencies fail.
scaleAssumptions: 1B events/day, 100k dashboard viewers, and 10k saved reports
Partition by the primary tenant, user, item, or geographic key and isolate hot partitions.
Keep serving state bounded; retain raw events or durable records for replay and auditing.

dataFlow.title: Register sources and contracts
dataFlow.description: The real time analytics dashboard catalog records owners, schemas, compatibility rules, retention, lineage, and partitioning before data is accepted.

dataFlow.title: Ingest with backpressure
dataFlow.description: Connectors checkpoint real time analytics dashboard source cursors, validate schema and deduplication keys, and slow producers when downstream capacity is exhausted.

dataFlow.description: Stream or batch engines compute real time analytics dashboard transformations using watermarks, late-data policy, state checkpoints, and deterministic code versions.

architecture.title: Real Time Analytics Dashboard data platform architecture
architecture.summary: Design a real-time analytics dashboard that ingests streaming events, maintains queryable aggregates, refreshes visualizations automatically, and controls analytical cost and freshness. The design preserves immutable source evidence and contracts, processes partitions with checkpointed batch or streaming jobs, and serves curated results with freshness and quality metadata.

layers.label: Data quality and cost operations
layers.description: Freshness, completeness, schema, lag, query, and pipeline-cost signals are actionable.

deepDives.title: Schema evolution and data quality
points: Version real time analytics dashboard contracts and make compatibility rules explicit for every producer and consumer.
Quarantine malformed partitions instead of poisoning the whole dataset.
Track row counts, null rates, duplicates, distribution changes, and policy violations by partition.

deepDives.title: Watermarks, late data, and exactly-once effects
points: Use source cursors and event-time watermarks for real time analytics dashboard progress, not wall-clock assumptions.
Make checkpoints, output keys, and sink commits retry-safe under at-least-once delivery.
Document how late events revise windows, aggregates, or snapshots.

deepDives.title: Replay, lineage, and cost
points: Keep immutable real time analytics dashboard raw evidence and code or schema versions so failed outputs can be reproduced.
Separate hot serving storage from cold retention and cap replay concurrency.
Measure freshness, backlog, compute cost, storage growth, and quality-gate failure rate.

tradeoffs.title: Streaming versus batch
tradeoffs.recommendation: Use streaming for freshness-critical real time analytics dashboard paths and batch for backfills, compaction, and expensive recomputation.
tradeoffs.caution: Forcing every workload into streaming makes state, replay, and cost harder to operate.

tradeoffs.title: Raw retention versus curated-only storage
tradeoffs.recommendation: Retain enough immutable raw evidence for replay, audit, and correction, then tier or expire it according to policy.
tradeoffs.caution: Without raw evidence, a bad transformation can require an unreproducible emergency fix.

tradeoffs.title: Central warehouse versus domain-owned datasets
tradeoffs.recommendation: Centralize governance and discovery while letting domain owners own contracts and quality signals.
tradeoffs.caution: A single team owning every transformation becomes a delivery bottleneck and hides data ownership.

commonMistakes: Treating real time analytics dashboard ingestion success as proof that downstream data is complete or correct.
Dropping late events or schema failures without a quarantine and replay path.
Using wall-clock processing time where event-time windows and watermarks are required.
Overwriting curated data in place without run, code, schema, or input lineage.
Ignoring backlog, freshness, quality, storage, and compute-cost signals until consumers report stale data.

followUps.question: How do you replay a failed real time analytics dashboard partition?
followUps.answer: Retain source cursor and watermark, rerun a versioned transformation into an isolated output, validate quality, then atomically publish the replacement.

followUps.question: How do you handle schema changes?
followUps.answer: Register a new version, validate compatibility, dual-read or dual-write when needed, and expose the active contract to consumers.

followUps.question: What does exactly once mean here?
followUps.answer: It means the combination of durable checkpoints, deterministic output identities, and idempotent sinks prevents duplicate business effects; transport alone remains at least once.

rubric.description: The answer addresses the real time analytics dashboard workflow, scale, latency, durability, authorization, and failure contract.
The answer identifies the authoritative real time analytics dashboard state, versioning or deduplication boundary, and how derived views converge.
The answer partitions real time analytics dashboard traffic, isolates hot keys, and moves fan-out, retries, or rebuilds behind bounded asynchronous work.
The answer names freshness, backlog, error, cost, and recovery signals tied to the real time analytics dashboard user experience.
